messages.author: ca31c2295ae7ae58
messages.subject: MSStatsPTM got stuck during Summarization of protein.data
parts:
Dear developers,

I have phosphoproteomics data analyses with Spectronaut 17 and run into an error during dataSummarizationPTM(). My setup is as follows: 
I have 4 treatments in 4 biological replicates each (=total 16 samples). From each sample I have the total sample (=proteome) and two phosphoenriched fractions (TiO2, FeNTA). The separate phospho fractions were actually generated by tandem-enrichment following Thermo's SMOAC-protocol, meaning that the flow trough of TiO2 was again run over a Fe-NTA-column. 
I now ran the samples trough Spectronaut in two separate searches, once only the total total 16 proteome samples, and once the 32 phosphosamples. In the later search I labeled the individual phosphofractions in Spectronaut with unique identifiers during the experimental setup (TiO2, FeNTA). I afterwards exported each search result into the long MSStsats report containing the following columns:  
> colnames(ptm_data)
 [1] "R.Condition"                  "R.FileName"                   "R.Replicate"                  "PG.ProteinAccessions"        
 [5] "PG.ProteinGroups"             "PG.Qvalue"                    "PG.Quantity"                  "PEP.GroupingKey"            
 [9] "PEP.StrippedSequence"         "PEP.Quantity"                 "EG.iRTPredicted"              "EG.Library"                  
[13] "EG.ModifiedSequence"          "EG.PrecursorId"               "EG.Qvalue"                    "FG.Charge"                  
[17] "FG.Id"                        "FG.PrecMz"                    "FG.Quantity"                  "F.Charge"                    
[21] "F.FrgIon"                     "F.FrgLossType"                "F.FrgMz"                      "F.FrgNum"                    
[25] "F.FrgType"                    "F.ExcludedFromQuantification" "F.NormalizedPeakArea"         "F.NormalizedPeakHeight"      
[29] "F.PeakArea"                   "F.PeakHeight"             

I first filtered out all features not containing a phospho-mod from the ptm-dataframe.Afterwards I additionally generated two annotation data frames:
ptm_annot and protein_annot (see attachment).
Conversion to MSStatsPTM-format using the dedicated converter went through without any error. But when I ran the summarization function afterwards, it got stuck at the protein summarization step. I am afraid this could have something to do with the size of my PTM table? Even after filtering for phosphor-only it has 7,748,064 rows. Maybe my MacBook Pro 16 i7 16 GB can simply not handle it? But on the other hand it got stuck during the protein summarization step which deals with a smaller number of rows.

Any help would be greatly appreciated,.

Best

Robert

messages.author: 13904eb0f06097b0
messages.subject: Re: MSStatsPTM got stuck during Summarization of protein.data
parts:
Hi Robert,

From your description it sounds like this is a DIA dataset with a lot of features per protein and the steps you took above were definitely the way to go.

The reason the protein dataset is taking longer is most likely due to the number of features per protein being very high. We do not usually run into this issue with the PTM dataset because we have a much lower feature count (e.g. the features have to span the same modification site).

In these cases, we recommend doing what you did and reducing the number of features. You should not see major analysis differences, and it will greatly decrease your processing time.

Additionally, in terms of the "Warning: Ran out of iterations and did not convergeWarning: Ran out of iterations and did not converge" message, I would not worry about this. This was caused by the summarization for a PTM not converging, most likely due to only having one (or two) features. As long as the summarized values make sense for your PTMs you should be good to go.

I think your analysis should work well with what you described above but definitely get back in touch if you continue to see problems.

Devon
